job.name: Choose the customer problem to act on
job.goal: Recommend what deserves action this week, using customer evidence and explicit tradeoffs.

rules.title: Show the source
rules.description: Cite source IDs for the recommended problem. Distinguish signal from counterevidence.

rules.title: Count customers, not just messages
rules.description: For every problem, report signal messages and distinct customer names separately. Repeated messages are not additional customers.

rules.title: Show what challenges the recommendation
rules.description: Include supplied counterevidence for the recommended problem and explain its implication.

rules.title: Do not let popularity hide severity
rules.description: Discuss every high or critical signal using its source ID. Explain the severity tradeoff, even when one customer is affected.

sources.text: Can you schedule our report export?
Following up on scheduled exports.
Our analyst still exports this manually.
Any update on export scheduling?
Our weekly report still takes manual work.
Checking again before the next reporting cycle.
The invitation expired before our teammate could join.
New teammates cannot tell which workspace they are joining.
We abandoned setup after the invite link failed.
Our admin had to restart the invitation flow twice.
We can use our existing script for now; this is inconvenient, not blocking.
Support got us through setup; the account is active now.
Deleting one project also removed another project. We cannot restore the missing work.
A dark theme would be easier on my eyes.
Please add dark mode.
I prefer dark interfaces.
Dark mode would be nice, but it is not blocking us.
I would like a dark theme.
This occurred once in our account; we have not reproduced it in a second workspace.
We can use the current theme without affecting our work.

decision.rationale: Exports have six customer requests, more than the four onboarding reports. The strongest demand is clear.

decision.recommendation: Fix invitation setup before scheduling exports.
decision.rationale: Four distinct customers report invitation friction. The six export messages come from one customer with a workaround. Harbor is now active, so four reports do not mean four currently blocked accounts.
decision.severityNote: The supplied signal reports are medium severity. There is no high or critical incident in this batch.

decision.rationale: Five distinct customers requested dark mode; only one reported deleted work. Customer breadth makes dark mode the priority. Maple can continue using the current theme.

decision.recommendation: Investigate deleted project recovery before starting dark mode.
decision.rationale: The critical report needs immediate investigation and containment, not an assumed full rewrite. Five customers request a cosmetic improvement; that breadth does not outweigh potential irreversible loss. Cedar has not reproduced it elsewhere, so scope remains unknown.
decision.severityNote: w2-01 describes critical lost work. Prioritize investigation and protect affected data. w2-07 limits our confidence about reach; verify reproduction before estimating the broader impact.

decision.recommendation: Act on the deleted-project data loss (data-loss). Although dark mode is far more popular, a critical, unrecoverable data-loss incident outranks a widely requested cosmetic preference.
decision.rationale: data-loss carries the only critical signal (w2-01): deleting one project also removed another and the work cannot be restored. This is severe and irreversible even though it comes from a single customer. dark-mode has more volume (5 signal messages from 5 distinct customers: w2-02, w2-03, w2-04, w2-05, w2-06), but every message is low severity and explicitly non-blocking (w2-05, and counterevidence w2-08). Per the 'do not let popularity hide severity' standard, the tradeoff favors the critical data-loss incident: potential permanent loss of customer work is a higher-order risk than an eye-comfort preference. The main caveat is reproducibility (see severity note and counterevidence).
decision.severityNote: w2-01 is the critical signal: cross-project deletion with unrecoverable work loss — the driver of this recommendation despite affecting one customer. w2-07 is high-severity counterevidence tied to the same problem: the incident occurred once in one account and has not been reproduced in a second workspace, so scope and root cause remain uncertain. Implication: prioritize investigation and a safeguard/backup path, but treat blast radius as unconfirmed pending reproduction. Note also that w2-01 (Cedar, Enterprise) and w2-07 (Cedar, Growth) share the name 'Cedar' but differ by segment; counted as one distinct signal customer for data-loss. All dark-mode signals are low severity.

lessons.text: Separate message count from customer count. Preserve counterevidence and weigh severity.
lessons.reason: One customer can send many messages; a single critical incident can outrank a popular preference.
